problems.title: Adding a predictive modality need not increase confidence for each sample
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Proposition 1 and Eq. (1), PDF p. 5.
claim: Paraphrase of Proposition 1: For a sample with modality set \(M\), any nested subsets \(B\subseteq C\subseteq M\), and any multimodal classifier, the confidence on \(x_B\) is strictly less than the confidence on \(x_C\), which is no greater than the confidence on \(x_M\) (Section 3.2, PDF page 5). The surrounding discussion assumes that all modalities are predictive and motivates a positive relationship between confidence and additional modalities for a reliable classifier. Equation (1)’s benefit uses a related confidence comparison.

The problem is the pointwise guarantee. Conditional entropy is an expectation over observations, and its monotonicity does not imply monotonic confidence on every observed sample. The counterexample uses a proper inclusion \(B\subset C=M\), so it does not depend on the strict inequality’s trivial failure when two subsets are equal.
analysis: Take a balanced binary label and two conditionally independent predictive signals with accuracies \(0.9\) and \(0.8\). Observing a positive first signal gives posterior \(0.9\) and odds \(9\). On the positive-probability event that the second signal is negative, its likelihood ratio is \(1/4\), so the posterior becomes \(9/(9+4)=9/13<0.9\). This is the exact calibrated Bayes classifier. Expected conditional entropy can improve while confidence decreases on an individual observation.
result: The stated universal pointwise confidence monotonicity is false even for informative modalities and calibrated prediction. This undermines that theoretical justification; it does not by itself measure the training strategy's utility.
repair: Replace the pointwise proposition by the average information inequality \(H(Y\mid X_C)\le H(Y\mid X_B)\), or weak average Bayes-accuracy monotonicity under its posterior assumptions. Neither result implies a per-sample confidence gate.
problems.impact_rationale: A calibrated Bayes counterexample refutes the universal pointwise confidence proposition used to justify the core modality-benefit construction. This substantial theoretical reasoning failure warrants Major, without claiming an empirical ranking reversal.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Released benefit scoring omits the confidence gate and changes the operational contribution scale
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, Eq. (1), PDF p. 5; Section 3.3, Eq. (4), PDF p. 6; Eq. (5), PDF p. 7.
claim: Eq. (1), Section 3.2, PDF p. 5, gates benefit on both correct prediction and the specified confidence comparison. Eq. (4), Section 3.3, PDF p. 6, defines contribution \(\Phi_m\), while Eq. (5), PDF p. 7, applies the weak-modality threshold \(\Phi_m\le1\). The released scoring omits that confidence gate and uses a rescaled contribution.
analysis: Omitting the confidence comparison changes eligibility for the benefit. Independently, a contribution rescaling \(c_m=\Phi_m/2\) requires changing the weak-modality threshold \(\Phi_m\le1\) to \(c_m\le1/2\). Retaining threshold one after rescaling changes decisions for \(1<\Phi_m\le2\). Neither operation is an equivalent rewriting of the stated gate and contribution units.

A shared linear-fusion realization has correct-class probabilities \(0.9\) for audio alone, \(0.8\) for visual alone and \(0.7\) for both. With log-odds \(L_A,L_V,L_F\), choose shared bias \(b=L_A+L_V-L_F\) and contributions \(L_A-b,L_V-b\). Both proper confidence comparisons fail, yet the current correctness-only scorer gives full benefit \(2\). When full confidence instead equals \(0.95\), the gate passes and paper contributions are \(2\), versus code scores \(1\); the loader adds a weak-modality copy at \(1\) but none at \(2\).
result: An architecture-realizable probability fixture changes the gate and augmentation branch; the historical table-producing implementation remains unidentified.
repair: A manuscript-faithful implementation needs an explicit policy for the comparison subset in Eq. (1), must compute the stated confidence gate, and must use the Eq. (4) contribution in units consistent with all subsequent transformations and thresholds. A normalized contribution \(c_m=\Phi_m/2\) can also be used, but the paper’s weak threshold \(\Phi_m\le1\) then becomes \(c_m\le1/2\). Every dependent branch, masking rule, and transformation must be expressed in the same units; changing a single displayed constant does not prove the whole strategy coherent.
problems.impact_rationale: An architecture-realizable probability fixture changes the gate and augmentation branch; the historical table-producing implementation remains unidentified.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: The released loop selects saved checkpoints using test-set accuracy
problems.source_location: Released CMoB.py, dataset construction at lines 273–291 and checkpoint selection at lines 356–387.
claim: This finding concerns the released procedure and its ability to supply an independent final evaluation. CMoB.py, lines 273–275, creates a training dataset, a second dataset named train_val_dataset using training mode, and a dataset using test mode. Lines 291 onward wrap the latter in test_dataloader. At line 356, each epoch calls the evaluation function with that test loader. Lines 358–359 compare the returned accuracy with best_acc; lines 361–387 construct and save a checkpoint when it improves.

The data route is not inferred from variable names alone. datasets/dataloader.py, lines 29–40, maps training mode to train.csv, validation mode to val.csv, and the remaining test route to test.csv. A separate validation branch exists. The function name valid does not change the fact that the actual argument is test_dataloader.
analysis: Using test-loader accuracy to decide when to save a checkpoint makes that set part of model selection. The selected score is consequently not an independent final-test assessment for this loop. The public snapshot does not prove that the paper's historical tables used exactly this selection path.

For two independent fixed models with population accuracy \(1/2\), selecting the larger correctness bit on one test example reports expected accuracy \(3/4\). Selection on independent validation instead leaves expected test accuracy \(1/2\). This establishes the mechanism, not its magnitude in CMoB.
result: Current source routes test.csv into checkpoint selection; the amount of selection optimism and historical table provenance are unknown.
repair: Select checkpoints using an independent validation set, then evaluate the selected model once on an untouched test set. No new training or corrected test accuracy is supplied.
problems.impact_rationale: Current source routes test.csv into checkpoint selection; the amount of selection optimism and historical table provenance are unknown.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

impact_rationale: A calibrated Bayes classifier with two predictive modalities violates the universal pointwise confidence proposition that motivates modality benefit. This is a substantial failure of the central theoretical justification, independently of the unmeasured benchmark effect.
